## [2026-06-12 16:30] — confidence-gated adaptive decode: joint-field thinker lifts accuracy above baseline; latency still above the tiny AR baseline

**TL;DR:** Built the adaptive two-tier pipeline (commits af57885, 0aa0e87): the thinker now diffuses scratchpad+answer as one joint field; chosen_token_confidence re-scores the field and rows whose minimum answer-token probability >= gate_confidence return the diffusion answer with zero AR steps; the rest escalate to the talker. Measured on 1000 unseen questions (1200-step models, CPU, 5 timed repeats): accuracy now clearly BEATS the baseline — 3-digit 0.998-1.000 vs 0.973, 5-digit 0.997 vs 0.980, stable across gates 0.5-0.999 — but wall-clock stays above the baseline: best 3-digit 74.7 ms vs 36.8 (2 diffusion steps, acc 0.999), best 5-digit comparable-accuracy point 128.1 ms vs 83.4 (3 steps, 0.992) or 167.3 ms at full accuracy 0.997. Fast-path fraction at gate 0.98: 20% (3d) / 30% (5d); gate 0.5 lifts it to 44%/57% with no accuracy loss. 31 tests pass, pyaot clean.

**Long description:** New pieces in tests/double_decoder.py: gate_confidence config field (default 0.98); chosen_token_confidence (one bidirectional forward, gather softmax prob of each chosen token); adaptive_decode (greedy joint-field diffusion, per-row min answer confidence, fast rows keep the diffusion answer slice, slow rows run talker_generate on the diffused scratchpad slice); run_adaptive_experiment (trains joint thinker on cat(think, answer), fraction talker, baseline; reports adaptive/diffusion-only/escalate-all/baseline accuracies + fast fraction). Proving tests written first (4): confidence shape/range, gate extremes (1.1 -> all escalate, 0.0 -> all fast), fast-path slice identity, experiment metric keys. Verbatim measurements: 3d baseline 36.8 ms acc 0.973; gates {0.5: 106.2 ms/0.998/fast 0.436, 0.9: 112.6/0.998/0.305, 0.98: 125.7/0.998/0.196, 0.999: 142.2/0.998/0.046, ds2@0.98: 74.7/0.999/0.196, ds3@0.98: 86.5/1.000/0.196}. 5d baseline 83.4 ms acc 0.980; gates {0.5: 167.3/0.997/0.573, 0.9: 187.0/0.997/0.405, 0.98: 197.6/0.997/0.295, 0.999: 229.7/0.997/0.100, ds2@0.98: 111.1/0.985/0.293, ds3@0.98: 128.1/0.992/0.295}.

**What worked:** Accuracy. The joint-field design plus escalation is the first variant to clearly beat the baseline at equal full training on the 1000-question eval (+2.5 points at 3 digits, +1.7 at 5); accuracy is flat across the whole gate sweep, meaning the confidence signal cleanly separates rows the diffusion answer already has right — the talker only fires where it adds value. At 5 digits, 2-step diffusion still scores 0.985 (> baseline 0.980) at 111.1 ms.

**What failed (the latency goal):** Adaptive remains 1.3-2x the baseline wall-clock despite the zero-AR fast path, for three measured reasons: (1) fast-path fraction is low at safe gates (20-30%) so most rows pay diffusion AND talker; (2) the diffusion pass set runs over prompt+think+answer (longer than the baseline's prompt+answer) with 6 (or 2-3) full-field forwards of a 2-layer model — against a 4-layer baseline decoding only answer_len tokens, the arithmetic only favors diffusion for much longer answers; (3) the baseline here is itself tiny, so per-forward Python/launch overhead dominates and parallel-decode savings cannot show. Do not conclude the fast-path idea fails in general — it fails at 4-6 token answers on a 137k-param AR competitor.

**What was kept / discarded:** Kept everything (adaptive_decode, chosen_token_confidence, run_adaptive_experiment, 4 tests, docs entries). gate_confidence default left 0.98; gate 0.5 measured equal-accuracy and faster, but one seed is not enough to relax a safety gate.

**Open questions / next steps:** (1) Longer answers (8+ digits or multi-operation problems) are where the fixed-pass diffusion fast path should overtake AR — the decisive experiment. (2) Escalation re-uses the full-field diffusion output; a cheap 1-2 step draft for gating plus full diffusion only on escalation could cut the common path further. (3) Fast-fraction is gate-limited, not capability-limited (diffusion-only accuracy at 3d was within 0.2 points of adaptive); a learned gate (small head trained on correctness) could double the fast fraction. (4) make lint still blocked repo-wide by foreign unformatted tests/test_clock_quantization.py (15:05 entry).
EOF
